Depends on if you have a shop do it or do it yourself probably could find the parts for pretty cheap on eBay

http://m.ebay.com/itm/Cast-Iron-Exhaust-Manifold-w-Gasket-Kit-for-Cherokee-Dakota-Truck-Wrangler-2-5L-/311008311973?nav=SEARCH Now I'm not sure how hard to access it is on your truck though so.

I can't see a reason to replace your entire exhaust manifold. That makes zero sense at all. I'd be very leery of that mechanic! Get a second opinion.

Based on what you said it sounds like you misfired and that caused the O2 sensor to trigger. I'd be looking more at why you are misfiring. I'd reset the codes and then drive it a bit longer - you won't hurt the engine. If the codes come back address them, starting with a new O2 sensor. If it continues you need to look at your ignition.

If you are misfiring you may have a compression problem. Open your oil fill cap while the engine is running. If exhaust is coming out of it you've got bad rings/pistons in one or more cylinders.

Yeah only reason to replace the exhaust manifold that I can think of is if it had a hole. The misfire could also be something on the ignition side of things - so if a coil is going bad or condensation got into the plug boots or something like that.

I believe those exhaust manifolds are prone to getting cracks but it might also just be loose. It'll be hard to tell for sure without digging in and taking some stuff apart. If it's just loose you might be able to get a wrench in there and snug up the bolts. There are videos on replacing them and you should also check out the popular jeep forums. Jeep folks are a pretty helpful and handy bunch - you might be able to find someone from a local jeep club that'll give you a hand in exchange for a case of beer.
